robots.description: An open-source ROS 2 robot from Ekumen, built to teach real robotics on a budget: two driven wheels and a caster, a spinning lidar on top, a Raspberry Pi for a brain. It is the first robot in the Robodex that RobotForge did not design — its spec here was read out of the official project's own files.

runs.source: Gate run 1 on scythe, 2026-10-26, build/gate-andino-1/gate-report.json — run verdict MARGINAL (motion vs ground truth PASS; odometry heading MARGINAL)
Gate run 2 on scythe, 2026-10-26, build/gate-andino-2/gate-report.json — run verdict FAIL (turn vs ground truth MARGINAL at 9.104 deg; odometry heading FAIL at 11.624 deg)

gate_status.note: Two recorded runs on scythe (2026-10-26), no PASS — recorded as measured; the locked thresholds were not touched. The drive is excellent in both runs (1.497% / 0.347% against ground truth, odometry distance error 0.003%), but the pivot turn is the failure mode: the robot is heavy (3.364 kg — the sum of the official URDF link masses) on two passive caster balls, so in a turn it physically under-rotates while its wheel odometry (perfect joint integration) over-reads heading by 8.285-11.624 degrees. The gate's own suspect line names wheel_separation / caster scrub. Diagnosis recorded; the verdict was not massaged.

robots.image_credit: Photo: Ekumen — the real robot, from the official Andino repository (docs/real_robot.png)

key_specs.battery: 3x 18650 Li-ion cells, ~11.1 V nominal (official BOM holder); capacity varies by cell — the spec uses 2600 mAh as a labelled estimate
key_specs.chassis: 0.25 m long x 0.10 m wide base deck (official URDF base.yaml); overall width 0.153 m across the wheels, wheel track 0.128 m
key_specs.ground_clearance: ~0.03 m — estimate; the URDF base plane rides at wheel radius (0.0331 m)
key_specs.height: ~0.18 m — estimate derived from the URDF deck stack
key_specs.mass: 3.364 kg — the sum of the official URDF link masses (several are round values upstream)
key_specs.motors: 2x DG01D-E gearmotors with encoders, 48:1 gearbox, rated 3-9 V (SparkFun listing linked from the official BOM), driven via an L298N
key_specs.sensors: RPLIDAR A1M8 2D lidar (top), Raspberry Pi Camera V2 (front), BNO055 IMU, wheel encoders
key_specs.wheels: 66.2 mm diameter x 25 mm — official wheel.yaml radius 0.0331 m

robots.description: ROBOTIS's small research-and-teaching rover: two driven wheels, a caster, and a 360-degree lidar. RobotForge's reference robot for the differential-drive layout — its spec here uses the public ROBOTIS reference dimensions.

gate_status.note: The same spec with --inject-wheel-scale 0.9 FAILS the gate (odometry error 11.168%, suspect wheel.diameter_m) — that injected run is a fault-injection demo, not this robot's clean status.

runs.source: P1 launch verification on scythe from a fresh clone of main, 2026-10-26 (project record: 'burger clean GATE PASS, drive 0.368%, odometry honest 0.042%')
Evidence run embedded in reports.html (burger-clean): drive 0.968%, turn 2.028 deg, all four checks PASS

Gate run on Torque's VM, 2026-10-28 — Gazebo Sim (Harmonic) with the gz-sim server embedded in-process, because the VM sandbox blocks the UDP transport the gate normally discovers over; verdict logic, thresholds and spec untouched. Full gate report: catalog/gate-runs/burger-torque-inprocess.json

robots.description: The PX4 ecosystem's reference quadcopter kit: a 500 mm X-frame, four 2216 920KV motors, a power-distribution board and a Pixhawk flight controller. RobotForge flies this exact airframe as the PX4 Gazebo model (x500), so its geometry here is read straight out of the model's own files.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots through a drive-and-turn maneuver in Gazebo and grades motion against ground truth; a flight gate does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Photo: ZLEA, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) — the Holybro X500 V2 kit

key_specs.Frame: X500 quadcopter frame, 500 mm wheelbase class (Holybro)
key_specs.Motor-to-motor: 0.348 × 0.348 m (0.492 m diagonal) — rotor positions in the PX4 Gazebo model
key_specs.Propellers: 0.279 m in the Gazebo model (the physical kit ships 1045 props)
key_specs.Mass: 2.064 kg — sum of the Gazebo model's link masses (base_link 2.0 kg + 4 rotors)
key_specs.Flight controller: Pixhawk, powered via PM02 power module
key_specs.Power: Power-distribution board documented: XT60 in, XT30 out

robots.name: PX4 X500

provenance.note: Geometry, height and link masses from the PX4 Gazebo model x500_base/model.sdf (rotor poses ±0.174 m, base_link pose z 0.24 m, link masses 2.0 kg + 4× 0.0160769 kg). Kit hardware (motors, ESCs, PDB wiring pattern, battery recommendation) from Holybro's official X500 V2 product page. The Gazebo model's propeller (0.279 m) differs from the physical kit's 1045 props; the model's value is what the spec carries, and the difference is stated in the key specs.
provenance.source_name: PX4/PX4-gazebo-models (x500_base SDF) + Holybro X500 V2 product page

robots.description: A quadcopter the size of your palm — 29 grams — where one circuit board is the frame, the flight controller and the power system at once. Bitcraze built it as a development platform you can fly indoors, and published everything about it.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots through a drive-and-turn maneuver in Gazebo and grades motion against ground truth; a flight gate does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Photo: Bitcraze — the Crazyflie 2.1+ on the official product site (the current revision of the 2.1 platform)

key_specs.Size: 92 × 92 × 29 mm — the datasheet measures this motor-to-motor, including the motor mount feet

robots.name: Crazyflie 2.1

provenance.license: Open-source hardware (design files and schematics published by Bitcraze)
provenance.note: Every value is from the official Crazyflie 2.1 datasheet (Rev 3): takeoff weight 29 g, size 92 × 92 × 29 mm measured motor-to-motor including motor mount feet, 250 mAh LiPo, 7 mm coreless motors, 47-17 propellers, BMI088 + BMP388. robots.description: Unitree's robot dog: four two-segment legs, twelve joint motors, a 4D LiDAR scanning unit in its head and a wide-angle camera. The Robodex's first legged entry — it walks, so the wheeled motion gate has nothing to grade it with yet.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots on wheels and grades drive/turn error; a walking gate for legged robots does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Photo: HotNews Romania – Adi Iacob, Ovidiu Popica, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

key_specs.Mass: 16.087 kg — sum of the URDF link masses; Unitree publishes ~15 kg with battery
key_specs.Battery: 8000 mAh smart battery; 28.8 V nominal (the table's 28–33.6 V band is an 8S pack; 33.6 V charger)
key_specs.Sensors: 4D LiDAR L1, HD wide-angle camera (Unitree parameter table)
key_specs.Wiring: Not documented publicly — no wiring block is shown for this robot

robots.name: Unitree Go2

provenance.note: Mass is the sum of the 33 link masses in the official go2_description URDF (body 6.923 kg + four legs at 2.291 kg each = 16.087 kg). That is more than Unitree's published ~15 kg with battery; the URDF models each joint's rotor as its own link, and the table's figure is a rounded marketing weight — both numbers are stated in the key specs and neither is hidden. Dimensions, motor count, battery and sensors from Unitree's published Go2 parameter table. The internal wiring harness is not publicly documented, so this spec carries no wiring block.
provenance.source_name: unitree_ros — go2_description URDF + Unitree Go2 published parameters

robots.description: A robot dog you build yourself: MangDang's open-source quadruped packs 12 servos and a Raspberry Pi into 560 g, and the whole design — CAD, code, docs — is published. The Robodex's smallest dog by far.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots on wheels and grades drive/turn error; a walking gate for legged robots does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Line illustration by RobotForge, drawn for this entry — not a photo (no linkable official photo of the v1 hardware exists)

key_specs.Battery: 800 mAh, 2S — 7.4 V nominal; MangDang's docs warn that over 8.4 V (over 2S) will fry the servos
key_specs.Structure mass note: The published URDF's link masses sum to just 0.304 kg — structure only; the servos, Pi and battery that make up the rest of the 560 g are not in the model

robots.name: Mini Pupper

provenance.note: Dimensions, weight, battery capacity and servo count from MangDang's published specifications (launch specification, as also reported by CNX Software and the Raspberry Pi magazine). The 2S / 7.4 V battery figure is from MangDang's own documentation ('battery spec… voltage should be less than 7.4 V'; over 8.4 V 'you'll almost certainly fry all your servos'). The description package's link masses (0.304 kg, structure only) are recorded in the key specs, not passed off as the robot's weight. No official v1 photo is linkable — the repository's photo shows the v2 — so this entry carries a labeled RobotForge line illustration instead.
provenance.source_name: MangDang — Mini Pupper published specifications, documentation, and mini_pupper_ros

robots.description: A 1.32 m humanoid with 29 powered joints, a depth camera and a 3D LiDAR in its head — the Robodex's first biped, and the biggest robot in it. Unitree publishes its dimensions and equipment; the mass breakdown here is grouped out of the official model files.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots on wheels and grades drive/turn error; a walking gate for legged robots does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

key_specs.Height (standing): 1320 mm; 450 mm wide, 200 mm deep (Unitree parameter table)
key_specs.Joints: 29 actuated joints — counted from the revolute joints in the official g1_29dof URDF
key_specs.Battery: 13-string lithium, 9000 mAh — 46.8 V nominal (54 V charger per the table)
key_specs.Sensors: Depth camera, 3D LiDAR (Unitree parameter table; both appear as links in the URDF)
key_specs.Wiring: Not documented publicly — no wiring block is shown for this robot

robots.name: Unitree G1

provenance.note: Dimensions, weight, battery and sensors from Unitree's published G1 parameter table (the table lists total DOF options up to 43 with optional arms; the base 29-DOF configuration is what the official g1_29dof URDF models). The URDF's 36 link masses sum to 35.115 kg, grouped in the spec as trunk 12.669 / legs 14.372 / arms 7.038 / head 1.036 kg — within half a percent of the published ~35 kg. Battery voltage 46.8 V is the 13-string nominal (the table's '13-string lithium battery' and 54 V charger imply it). The internal wiring harness is not publicly documented, so this spec carries no wiring block.
provenance.source_name: unitree_ros — g1_29dof URDF + Unitree G1 published parameters

robots.description: ROBOTIS's open humanoid research platform — the robot that plays in RoboCup demos: twenty Dynamixel servos on one daisy-chained bus, an OpenCR board running them, and a small PC for a brain. Half a metre tall, fully documented in the ROBOTIS e-Manual.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots on wheels and grades drive/turn error; a walking gate for legged robots does not exist yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Photo: ROBOTIS — the OP3 on the official e-Manual

key_specs.Actuators: 20× XM430-W350-R Dynamixel servos — legs 6 each, arms 3 each, head 2
key_specs.Stall torque: 3.8 N·m at 11.1 V (XM430-W350 e-Manual page; documented input 10.0–14.8 V)
key_specs.Battery: LiPo 3-cell, 11.1 V, 3300 mAh (current e-Manual; earlier ROBOTIS pages list 1800 mAh)
key_specs.Computing: Intel NUC (i3) + OpenCR sub-controller; Logitech C920 camera
key_specs.Footprint: ESTIMATED — ROBOTIS does not publish a standing footprint; the spec's 0.20 × 0.13 m is an estimate and is labeled as one

robots.name: ROBOTIS OP3

provenance.note: Height, weight, DOF, actuator model and battery from the ROBOTIS e-Manual OP3 introduction (the current e-Manual lists a 3300 mAh battery; older ROBOTIS material says 1800 mAh — the current figure is used and the change is noted). Stall torque and voltage range from the e-Manual's XM430-W350 page. The DOF split (legs 6 each, arms 3 each, head 2) is the e-Manual's 20-DOF layout as also published in RoboCup materials. ROBOTIS publishes no standing footprint: the spec's length and width are ESTIMATED from the robot's proportions and are labeled ESTIMATED everywhere they appear.
provenance.source_name: ROBOTIS e-Manual — OP3 introduction + XM430-W350 specification

robots.description: A tabletop robot arm from ROBOTIS: five Dynamixel servos — four arm joints and a gripper — on a TTL multidrop bus, with 380 mm of reach and a 500 g payload. It never moves from its base plate, and it has no battery at all: a 12 V supply plugs into the wall.

gate_status.note: Not gated. The motion gate drives ground robots and grades drive/turn error; there is no manipulation gate yet, so this entry carries no verdict — its spec is validated, and that is all that is claimed.

robots.image_credit: Photo: ROBOTIS — the OpenManipulator-X on the official e-Manual

key_specs.Actuators: 5× XM430-W350-T Dynamixel servos, TTL multidrop bus
key_specs.Weight: 0.70 kg — the e-Manual figure excludes the base plate; the URDF's link masses sum to 0.594 kg
key_specs.Power: 12 V DC supply — no onboard battery

robots.name: OpenManipulator-X

provenance.note: Actuators, input voltage, DOF, payload, weight, reach and gripper stroke all from the ROBOTIS e-Manual's OpenManipulator-X specification page. The e-Manual states the 0.70 kg weight excludes the base plate; the official URDF's seven link masses sum to 0.594 kg, recorded in the spec's component masses. The spec's width is the gripper's maximum stroke (75 mm) and its height the radial reach — an arm has no body box; both are labeled with what they mean. Power is a 12 V DC supply, modeled in the spec's battery slot with chemistry 'dc_supply' and zero capacity, because the arm carries no battery.
provenance.source_name: ROBOTIS e-Manual — OpenManipulator-X specification + ROBOTIS-GIT/open_manipulator URDF
